chunks: Harun ibn Muslim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Salih ibn Abdillah who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'My brother was detained, so I made it upon myself to fast for a month. I fasted, and sometimes some of my brothers would come to break the fast with me, so I broke the fast for a few days. Should I make it up?' He said, 'There is no harm.'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report indicates that when continuity is not stipulated, it is permissible for him to divide (the fasts).
ai.seo_question: Can I make up a vowed month of fasts non-consecutively if I broke them occasionally?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the flexibility in fulfilling voluntary vows (nadhr) when social obligations, such as hosting guests, arise. The jurist Muhammad ibn al-Hasan derives the principle that unless continuous fasting (tatabu') is explicitly stipulated, the missed days can be made up individually, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease and practicality in worship. This ruling underscores the balance between personal devotion and communal duties in Shia jurisprudence.
